title: Bluebridge Logistics
overview: Bluebridge Logistics is a freight company with headquarters in Rotterdam and regional offices in Lisbon and Warsaw. It's moving its line-of-business applications to Azure.
The company has one Microsoft Entra tenant with Microsoft Entra ID P1 licenses for all employees. Users are synchronized from an on-premises Active Directory domain.
existingEnvironment: Three subscriptions: Sub-Prod, Sub-Dev and Sub-Shared. All are currently directly under the tenant root group.
A group named IT-Ops contains the central operations team.
Each regional office has a small help desk team.
Storage account stbbdocs (Standard GPv2, LRS) holds shipping documents in a container named manifests.
requirements: Production subscriptions must only allow resources in West Europe and North Europe; development subscriptions may use any region. The rule must apply automatically to new production subscriptions.
Each regional help desk must be able to reset passwords only for users in its own office.
Every resource must carry a CostCenter tag. Resources that inherit from their resource group should be tagged automatically.
Shipping documents must remain readable if a single datacenter in the region fails. Cost must be minimized.
Use least privilege and minimize administrative effort.

title: Harborview Clinics
overview: Harborview Clinics operates 12 outpatient clinics and a central datacenter. It's deploying a patient portal and internal services to Azure in the East US region.
Security and compliance teams require private connectivity to data services and strict network segmentation.
existingEnvironment: Hub VNet vnet-hub (10.0.0.0/16) contains a VPN gateway connected to the datacenter (172.20.0.0/16) by site-to-site VPN.
Spoke VNets vnet-portal (10.10.0.0/16) and vnet-data (10.20.0.0/16) are peered with vnet-hub.
The patient portal runs on VMs in vnet-portal behind a web tier. Patient documents are stored in storage account sthvdocs.
Clinic staff connect over the internet from clinic sites; administrators work from the datacenter.
requirements: The portal must route /api/* requests to API servers and all other requests to web servers, and must be protected against common web exploits.
VMs in both spokes must reach the datacenter through the existing VPN gateway; no additional gateways may be deployed.
sthvdocs must not be reachable from the internet. Datacenter servers and VMs in both spokes must access it using private IP addresses.
Administrators must manage VMs over RDP/SSH without public IP addresses on VMs.

title: Summit Outdoor Retail
overview: Summit Outdoor Retail runs its e-commerce platform on Azure VMs in Central US, with a secondary region of East US 2.
The operations team is small and wants automated monitoring and recovery wherever possible.
existingEnvironment: Web and order-processing VMs run Windows Server in Central US.
A Log Analytics workspace law-ops exists in Central US.
No backups or disaster recovery are configured.
requirements: The on-call engineer must receive an SMS and email when any web VM's CPU stays above 90% for 15 minutes; the same contacts are used for all critical alerts.
Notifications must be suppressed during the weekly maintenance window on Sunday 01:00–03:00 without modifying alert rules.
VMs must be backed up daily with 30-day retention; individual files must be restorable without restoring entire VMs.
If Central US becomes unavailable, the order-processing tier must be running in East US 2 within one hour, starting the database VMs before the application VMs.
